correctness.rationale: The exact 4-composition formula enumerates every lattice point in the prescribed fibers and determines each numerator coefficient by a finite binomial transform. Gorenstein symmetry restricts complete strict log-concavity to 3m adjacent minors; all were evaluated with exact integers for m=1,...,11, using an exhaustive finite checker. The source first-three-coefficient identities and direct enumerations agree; Q_m>0 was checked exactly at m=12,...,20. For m>=21, explicit universal inequalities give h1>=8^m/2, h3>=216^m/2 and 0<=h2<=10*36^m, hence Q_m>=1728^m/4-100*1296^m>0. The three requisite exponential inequalities hold at 21 and propagate by induction. Every quantifier is covered; numerical tests are not extrapolated to infinity.

originality.rationale: The original full paper defines the same R_m and shows the failure at m=12, but does not prove strict log-concavity of every coefficient for 1<=m<=11 or permanent index-two failure for every m>=12. The first half is a finite exhaustive result not entailed by one witness; the second half requires an infinite-range exponential estimate. Relevant published mathematical records, preceding results on Gorenstein unimodality, and recoverable earlier claims were compared on implications. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: This identifies the sharp first loss of the stronger log-concavity property across an explicitly motivated family of Gorenstein index-four IDP polytopes with regular unimodular flag triangulations. The source gives only one failure member; the result adds a complete positive phase and a permanent failure phase, resolving when the phenomenon first appears in that canonical family. It does not misrepresent this as an absolute dimension-minimal counterexample across all Gorenstein polytopes.
